title: Tenant sandboxing and multiplexed transport for private observability collectors
creator: Aisha Reynolds
description: Introduce a tenant sandboxing layer and a multiplexed transport for VPC/on‑prem collectors to safely cohost multiple customers on a single collector instance while preserving isolation, auditability, and observable SLA signalling. This ticket designs and implements the core runtime and control-plane hooks (lease reconciliation, per-tenant queueing, signed envelope validation, and multiplexed gRPC/HTTP streams) plus dashboards for latency/error attribution by tenant for Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Collector can accept multiplexed streams where a single connection carries telemetry for multiple tenant IDs and correctly demultiplex into isolated processing queues
Per-tenant sandbox guarantees: CPU/memory soft limits, request rate quotas, and per-tenant error isolation without cross-tenant amplification
Signed envelope validation for on‑prem collectors implemented with audit logs and configurable enforcement (warn|reject)
Lease reconciliation process prevents stale tenant routing entries for at least 99.9% of churn windows and recovers within configured TTL
Latency and error dashboards in Console surface per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and dropped-sample counts for Private/Dedicated only
E2E tests simulate noisy-tenant scenarios and demonstrate no >2x latency amplification for neighbor tenants under full load
implementation_plan: Design multiplexed transport protocol: header schema (tenant-id, stream-id, sequence, envelope-signature), backpressure markers, and reconnect semantics
Add sandboxing layer in collector process: per-tenant worker pool, cgroups/rlimit integration for on-prem, and soft-kill policies
Implement signed-envelope validator hook that can be toggled between permissive and strict modes via config and feature flag
Build lease-reconciler subservice to manage tenant routing entries from control plane and reconcile with local state on reconnect
Instrument per-tenant metrics (ingest-rate, parse-errors, processing-latency, queue-depth) and emit tags for Console ingestion
Ship a lightweight dashboard template and a runtime SLO rule bundle to Console for private deployments
Run chaos experiments and noisy-tenant load tests on a dedicated staging cluster and iterate on circuit-breaker thresholds
progress_updates: 2025-01-15: Kickoff meeting with Platform, Security, and PM. Agreed scope covers transport + sandbox + dashboards. Action: produce protocol draft.
2025-01-24: Protocol draft v0.1 reviewed; Security flagged envelope-signature key distribution as high risk. Assigned follow-up: KMS integration feasibility (ENG-41207 referenced).
2025-02-02: PoC multiplexed gRPC stream implemented in collector prototype. Basic demux and per-tenant queueing present. Observed 18% CPU overhead under moderate load.
2025-02-08: Design review with Console team. Agreed telemetry tags and metrics schema. Console will add per-tenant dashboard template (PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/1128).
2025-02-14: Security review in progress; temporary decision to ship validator in warn mode with audit logging for initial rollout. Strict enforcement gated on KMS/HSM rollout.
2025-02-20: Load tests: simulated noisy tenant causes neighbor queue latency increase of 1.6x. Tuned worker pool and backpressure markers to bring neighbor amplification below 2x.
decisions: Use multiplexed single-connection transport to reduce connection explosion for on-prem proxies and simplify firewall rules for customers.
Sandboxing implemented as soft resource controls (worker pools + soft rlimits) rather than strict containerization to reduce operational complexity for on-prem installers.
Envelope validation will default to 'warn' on initial rollout; strict reject mode requires KMS integration and separate migration ticket.
Per-tenant metrics will be exported as tags rather than separate metric series to keep cardinality manageable in Console.
Lease reconciliation uses a TTL-backed optimistic cache with periodic control-plane reconciliation every 30s; acceptable trade for reduced control-plane pressure.
risks: Key distribution for signed envelopes remains the highest security risk; without HSM/KMS integration strict enforcement is difficult.
Multiplexing increases complexity of failure modes (partial stream failure affecting multiple tenants); need robust reconnection/backoff strategy.
Metrics cardinality could increase if tenant tags are used naively; must rely on aggregated buckets for high-cardinality tenants.
On‑prem environments with limited resource isolation may still experience noisy-neighbor effects despite sandboxing; document deployment best-practices.
test_plan: Unit tests for demultiplexer, envelope validator, and lease reconciler
Integration test: single collector with 500 simulated tenants using multiplexed streams
Stress test: 5 noisy tenants producing 1000 rps each while verifying neighbor p95 latency remains within SLO
Security test: replay attack simulation to verify envelope sequence checks and TTL enforcement
E2E: deploy to a private staging cluster and exercise dashboard ingestion and SLO alerting
notes: Follow-up ticket required to plumb KMS-based key rotation into envelope validator; target ENG-78002.
Consider an optional 'tenant-sharding' helper on control-plane to reduce lease churn for very large customers.
Customer docs: add 'on-prem sizing guide' and recommended firewall/NAT settings for multiplexed transport installs.
